body.statement: The frontier theorem is equivalent, up to fixed constants, to \[R_T(B)\asymp\begin{cases}b^{-\alpha},&\alpha<1,\\ b^{-1}+T^{-1}\log(1+b),&\alpha=1,\\ b^{-\alpha}+T^{-1},&\alpha>1.\end{cases}\]
body.justification: The three regimes display when capacity, multiscale deadline accumulation, or the mandatory final pair determines regret.
body.gap: Adjacent papers report dimension-specific matching rates but do not derive this smoothness-by-dimension phase transition under a hard experimental reservoir.
body.consumer: The regime table converts a theorem into sample-size and memory guidance for trial planning.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an even \(T\ge 32\) and \(B\ge 1\).  Then \(b=\min\{B,T/2\}\) is an integer satisfying \(1\le b\le T/2\), and \(\alpha=2\beta/d>0\).  Put
\[
H_\alpha(b)=\sum_{r=1}^{b}r^{-\alpha}.
\]
By Definition~\(\mathrm{def:frontier}\),
\[
F_\alpha(T,b)=b^{-\alpha}+T^{-1}H_\alpha(b). \tag{1}
\]

Suppose first that \(0<\alpha<1\).  Because \(r^{-\alpha}\ge b^{-\alpha}\) for every \(1\le r\le b\), and because \(x\mapsto x^{-\alpha}\) is nonincreasing,
\[
b^{1-\alpha}=b b^{-\alpha}
\le H_\alpha(b)
\le 1+\int_1^b x^{-\alpha}\,dx
=1+\frac{b^{1-\alpha}-1}{1-\alpha}
\le \left(1+\frac{1}{1-\alpha}\right)b^{1-\alpha}. \tag{2}
\]
Let \(K_\alpha=1+(1-\alpha)^{-1}\).  Since \(b/T\le 1/2\), (1)--(2) imply
\[
b^{-\alpha}
\le F_\alpha(T,b)
\le b^{-\alpha}+K_\alpha T^{-1}b^{1-\alpha}
=\left(1+K_\alpha\frac bT\right)b^{-\alpha}
\le \left(1+\frac{K_\alpha}{2}\right)b^{-\alpha}. \tag{3}
\]
Thus \(F_\alpha(T,b)\asymp b^{-\alpha}\) when \(0<\alpha<1\).

Suppose next that \(\alpha=1\).  Monotonicity of \(x\mapsto x^{-1}\) gives
\[
\log(1+b)=\int_1^{b+1}\frac{dx}{x}
\le H_1(b)
\le 1+\int_1^b\frac{dx}{x}
=1+\log b
\le \left(1+\frac{1}{\log 2}\right)\log(1+b), \tag{4}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(b\ge1\), hence \(1\le \log(1+b)/\log 2\).  Substitution into (1) yields
\[
b^{-1}+T^{-1}\log(1+b)
\le F_1(T,b)
\le b^{-1}+\left(1+\frac{1}{\log 2}\right)T^{-1}\log(1+b). \tag{5}
\]
Consequently,
\[
F_1(T,b)\asymp b^{-1}+T^{-1}\log(1+b). \tag{6}
\]

Finally, suppose that \(\alpha>1\).  The first summand and the integral comparison give
\[
1\le H_\alpha(b)
\le 1+\int_1^\infty x^{-\alpha}\,dx
=1+\frac{1}{\alpha-1}. \tag{7}
\]
Writing \(K'_\alpha=1+(\alpha-1)^{-1}\), equations (1) and (7) give
\[
b^{-\alpha}+T^{-1}
\le F_\alpha(T,b)
\le b^{-\alpha}+K'_\alpha T^{-1}
\le K'_\alpha\{b^{-\alpha}+T^{-1}\}, \tag{8}
\]
because \(K'_\alpha>1\).  Hence \(F_\alpha(T,b)\asymp b^{-\alpha}+T^{-1}\) when \(\alpha>1\).

Define
\[
\Phi_\alpha(T,b)=
\begin{cases}
b^{-\alpha},&0<\alpha<1,\\
b^{-1}+T^{-1}\log(1+b),&\alpha=1,\\
b^{-\alpha}+T^{-1},&\alpha>1.
\end{cases}
\]
Equations (3), (5), and (8) show that there are constants \(0<k_\alpha\le K_\alpha^\star<\infty\), independent of \(T\), \(B\), and \(b\), such that
\[
k_\alpha\Phi_\alpha(T,b)
\le F_\alpha(T,b)
\le K_\alpha^\star\Phi_\alpha(T,b). \tag{9}
\]
Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:minimax\text{-}frontier}\) supplies constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) for which
\[
cF_\alpha(T,b)\le R_T(B)\le CF_\alpha(T,b). \tag{10}
\]
Combining (9) and (10) gives
\[
ck_\alpha\Phi_\alpha(T,b)
\le R_T(B)
\le CK_\alpha^\star\Phi_\alpha(T,b), \tag{11}
\]
which is exactly the displayed three-regime assertion.  Conversely, any two-sided bound of the form \(c'\Phi_\alpha(T,b)\le R_T(B)\le C'\Phi_\alpha(T,b)\), together with (9), implies
\[
\frac{c'}{K_\alpha^\star}F_\alpha(T,b)
\le R_T(B)
\le \frac{C'}{k_\alpha}F_\alpha(T,b). \tag{12}
\]
Thus the regime display and the two-sided frontier bounds are equivalent up to fixed multiplicative constants.
